articles.title: Ebon Moss-Bachrach in Final Talks for Heat 2 Role
articles.summary: The Bear’s Ebon Moss-Bachrach is reportedly in final talks to join Michael Mann’s Heat 2 as Kelso, according to TheWrap. Kelso is the mysterious former DARPA researcher and hacker who furnishes Neil McCauley character with the intel he needs to take down his scores.
body: The two-time Emmy winner will join a stacked cast, including Leonardo DiCaprio as Chris Shiherlis (originally played by Val Kilmer), Christian Bale as Detective Vincent Hanna (originally played by Al Pacino), and Stephen Graham in Robert De Niro’s old role as Neil McCauley.

Heat 2, which was first released as a novel by Mann and thriller author Meg Gardiner in 2022, serves as both a prequel and a sequel to the events of the original film, which is widely considered to be one of the greatest heist films of all time. Mann has wanted to turn Heat 2 into a movie for some time, resolving in 2023 that he was planning for the project to be his next film.
While the original film was made with Warner Bros., Heat 2 has since ended up at Amazon MGM Studios.

articles.title: PlayStation Wants You to Use Your Controller to Simplify Payments
articles.summary: Near Field Communication, commonly known as NFC, has simplified card transactions, greatly speeding up the payment process. According to a recently filed patent, Sony wants to bring NFC to its DualSense controllers in order to enable faster PlayStation purchases.
body: Every player who uses a controller knows how much effort it takes to type using the D-pad and analog stick. You have to go through this process when entering passwords or adding card information. Most phones on the market feature NFC, which allows users to hold their device near a payment terminal to complete a transaction. This comes in particularly handy when making everyday purchases, as it eliminates the need to pull out your wallet, insert the card into the machine, and enter your passcode. Sony also wants to simplify the payment process on console by adding NFC to PlayStation controllers.

With this technology, players would be able to complete a purchase simply by holding their phone or card near the DualSense. But that's not all — if you were able to easily connect your phone to the console, it would also open the door for all sorts of data transfers via NFC.

articles.title: 5 Essential Backrooms Videos to Watch on YouTube After the Movie
articles.summary: Taken together, the YouTube videos do connect, though not always in particularly useful ways — and they might help you deepen your understanding of the movie. A 30-second clip called 9780415263573, for instance, appears to be highway-camera footage of a car disappearing.
body: Most of Parsons’ YouTube shorts are snippets that elliptically suggest a larger story without actually telling it, and many end in the middle of a scene, before resolving whatever is happening. Unlike traditional found-footage horror, which creators generally style as unearthed video that somehow contains a complete story, Parsons’ uploads truly feel like unanchored digital remnants recovered from a discarded, corrupted hard drive. Watch them all and you can piece together the beginnings of a narrative. In the later videos especially, a few characters persist from one installment to another, and the contours of a larger story start to emerge. But that story still hasn’t been fully told.

Still, if you’re new to the Backrooms phenomenon, loved the movie, and want more — or if you just want the best taste of the online work that inspired boutique studio A24 to pursue Parsons for a feature film — these are the five essential videos from his Backrooms series.

articles.title: PlayStation Reportedly Polling Game Developers After Decision to Kill Discs Sparks Backlash
articles.summary: PlayStation is reportedly sending a lengthy survey to game developers with a question about how they sell physical games after their decision to stop producing physical game discs prompted intense backlash.
body: The death of physical discs will not happen quietly; fans are making their voices heard as loudly as possible, to the point where PlayStation itself is reportedly reaching out to game developers asking for their thoughts on the divisive subject.

Speaking on the Broken Silicon Podcast, content creator, writer, and showrunner Tom claimed that he’d been made aware of a survey making the rounds among game developers from Sony. His sources claimed that it was possibly the longest survey that Sony has ever distributed.

“There is a survey Sony sent out to developers that is, what I was told by my contacts, a bigger survey than they’ve sent almost ever before, if not ever before. And there was a question in it basically trying to ask in a not-direct way, ‘Is there an issue with how we sell games physically?’ or something, like asking developers for feedback on killing discs.

“ Wolverine is still selling plenty of physical copies, and you’ve also got Sony starting to ask devs if they are worried about killing physical [discs], suggesting they realize that if they got a bunch of feedback, maybe they would consider some sort of mea culpa on it. We’ll see.”

articles.title: 29 Years Later, Charlie Brown's Wisest Quote Is Still an All-Time 'Peanuts' Classic
articles.summary: By now, 26 years after the strip ended, Peanuts often feels like it comes pre-digested. Even during its original run, much of Peanuts got carefully filtered through layers of T-shirts, greeting cards, and inspirational wall posters.
body: When you actually read the strip for itself, it can be a surprise to find that Peanuts, particularly in the first half of its run, has more of an edge than it gets credit for. In fact, what put it on the map in the first place was how Charles Schulz depicted childhood. At a point when many other cartoonists focused on the nostalgic joys of being a kid, Schulz wrote about its confusions and quiet terrors.

It's often forgotten now, after decades of enshrinement in the American pop-cultural canon, but this is easily the most subversive element of the strip. Peanuts is frequently a meditation on how rough it really is to be a little kid, which made it a strong counterpoint to the more saccharine vibes of 1950s newspaper gag comics.

articles.summary: Arc Raiders developer Embark Studios is bowing to the pacifists and trialing a PvE mode in their extraction shooter. If you play between October 13th and 20th, you'll be able to flick a toggle that means you load either into the traditional world of Arc Raiders, where human players vie for the…
body: "We’re seeing a large and growing group of Raiders who come to the Rust Belt for the co-op and the ARC, not fighting with other Raiders," Embark say in the post announcing the trial. "That group has become a core part of our community, so it’s important we learn how to support them properly rather than leave them working around the game."

To back this up, the studio share some data they've collected, showing that there are now more players that play only friendly co-op and never attack other humans than the merciless pure PvP bunch. Apparently the PvP group has remained at a stable 34% since the game's launch, but the number of mixed players, who spend most their time being affable members of the post-apocalypse society but occasionally dabble in wanton homicide, has shrunk, with most opting to become full-time peaceniks.

articles.title: My first MMO character #6: Jacob Ridley
articles.summary: My first MMO character was... Don L Legs. Born: [I was a small child] Game: RuneScape. My memories from this time are hazy at best. If this is all bollocks to a seasoned RuneScape player, this is at least what I thought was happening at the time.
body: I got really good at fishing. Like, really good. I was top level or something like that. Fishing and cooking. I used my skills to trade cooked fish with higher level players, and they'd give me good armour. I always wanted the black armour with golden highlights, whatever that was, and I got it by becoming a virtual fishmonger. I also got a red face mask and a black halberd. It was wicked.

One day, I just stopped playing. You don't realise it's the last time you'll play, but it was—at least for a very long time. I always kept my account details, though. Not too long ago, in 2025, I decided to log back in after God knows how many years. I'm 34 now, but I was 33 then. I must've been 10 or under when I was playing RuneScape.

I was banned. My account had been banned for years. Some clown had stolen it and used it to do nefarious things in my name. I don't know why, but I felt a real sadness for losing that account, even despite not logging in for years. So I sent Jagex an email.

articles.title: Arc Raiders Is Testing a PvE Mode Very Soon
articles.summary: Embark Studios has announced that it will be testing a PvE mode for Arc Raiders next month. From October 13 to October 20, Arc Raiders will have a PvE toggle, allowing you to seamlessly switch between lobbies where you can fight other players and lobbies where players can't do damage to you.
body: Embark will be monitoring the player economy and matchmaking times during this period. The team has noted that "it's possible that this will not work," meaning PvE may not actually make its way into the game permanently. This is a test to see how well they can make it'll operate, rather than some kind of stress test.

"It’s important to mention that this is not a risk-free test," said the studio. "The first, unlaunched iteration of ARC Raiders was conceived as a PvE game, and we have been hesitant to return to that concept. There is a risk that introducing a PvE matchmaking toggle could reduce some of the tension that the game was built around. At the same time, we have to respect that some players want to enjoy the game in their own way, and we can’t ignore what the data is telling us.

"As creators, we design a game with an intention for how we think it should be played; but after launch, it becomes the players’ game. This is one of the unique and wonderful things about making games; we build something with a specific vision, and then we get to see players finding their own ways to enjoy it."

articles.title: 2026’s Most Inventive Sci-Fi Thriller Is Officially Making Its Streaming Debut
articles.summary: If 2026 has proven anything, it's that horror filmmaking is firing on all cylinders. Earlier in the year, Curry Barker dissected modern intimacy through the nightmare lens of Obsession, while Damian McCarthy built a masterclass in spatial dread and folklore with Hokum.
body: None, however, have topped the liminal nightmare of Kane Parsons’ Backrooms. A film that translated internet mythos into a box-office-shattering theatrical event, it transposes the eerie familiarity of fluorescent-lit architecture into pure terror, and it’s finally streaming on HBO Max starting today, Sept. 25. Whether you missed the film’s big-screen run or simply want to get lost in its endless fluorescent maze again, it remains the essential home-viewing release of the season for horror aficionados.

Chiwetel Ejiofor stars as Clark, a struggling furniture store owner whose life has not gone quite the way he had expected. During an exploration of the basement beneath his store, Clark discovers a strange crack in the wall that leads into a seemingly infinite maze of interconnected spaces. At first, the discovery feels almost like an impossible gift. Clark begins documenting and mapping the space, stealing some of the furniture within while attempting to understand the strange world he stumbled into. But the deeper Clark goes, the clearer it becomes that the Backrooms are not simply an architectural curiosity.

articles.title: In Saraab: Beyond The Veil, Your Inner Demons Are Coming For You This November
articles.summary: Anyone looking for a creepy adventure to play in November will want to check out Saraab: Beyond the Veil. Solo developer Lubna Ahmed has announced a November 3 release date for the game on PC via Steam and Itch.io, and a demo will be available for it during the October edition of Steam Next Fest.
body: An Arabian folklore-inspired horror visual-novel game, Saraab follows Elham, a schoolgirl whose brother has suddenly been kidnapped. Rescuing your sibling means confronting your own inner demons, who have been externalized as monsters born of Elham's own psyche. To overcome them, she'll have to unlock the powers of her bloodline and uncover the truth of who she truly is.

"I'm incredibly excited to bring this story to players and share a world shaped by authentic cultural themes, folklore, and emotional experiences that are rarely explored in games," Ahmed said in a press statement. "I hope players everywhere can connect with the game's story and characters, because ultimately, it's a story about the human heart."

articles.title: Nintendo Reportedly Canceled A Ubisoft-Developed Zelda Game Starring Ganondorf
articles.summary: Zelda fans have had no shortage of new games to play in recent years, but it appears that one game--starring the franchise's iconic villain--was also in the works at one point. Rather than having Nintendo internally develop the game, however, the project was in the works at Ubisoft.
body: In a September 24 report, Insider Gaming says that Ubisoft Milan was working on a Zelda spin-off with the internal name "Goliath," which was set to star a new protagonist. During the early period of development, this was changed to have longtime big bad Ganondorf be the playable character. Outside of the Super Smash Bros. series, this would be a first and would presumably be quite different from other Zelda games.

However, the report says that Nintendo "rejected the prototype" back in late 2023, and the team--including Davide Soliani, who directed the Mario + Rabbids games--opted to leave Ubisoft and form their own studio, Day 4 Night, which is currently developing Bradley the Badger. This occurred despite Ubisoft's attempts to pitch Nintendo on a different IP in its place, with both Star Fox and Mario mentioned, but it wasn't meant to be.
It isn't the first time a Zelda spin-off has been canceled, apparently, with Retro Studios' Sheik-focused Project X reportedly getting canned during the Wii's lifespan.

articles.title: Steam’s Punk Games Showcase Hates AI Slop, Loves Blowing Up Nazis
articles.summary: Punks are taking over Steam starting on October 9 with the Punk Games Showcase, a week-long, curated digital festival celebrating games made with and expressing a punk spirit.
body: Over 400 games were submitted for consideration, and the final list includes over 100, with the intention of filtering out any that included generative AI, among other factors. Many featured games have already been released, while others are still to come. A few of them are even out this month or during the event.

Brad Smith of studio Miracle Tea, the creators of Club Soko, has been involved in itch.io's Hardcore Punk Jam since 2018, and is organizing the Steam showcase that will run alongside the game jam's latest edition.

Smith said the showcase has a few simple goals: to highlight games that "feature this style of music, are about the subculture, or are from creators who understand this scene, and it shows significantly in their games." He also hopes the showcase will influence Valve to add a "punk" categorization label on Steam, so developers can tag their games accordingly and players can find them more easily.
I caught up with Smith for more insight into the upcoming showcase and the movement to uplift games that wear their punk roots.

videos.title: FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE – Tokyo Game Show Trailer – Nintendo Switch 2
videos.summary: Pre-order and play the free demo for FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE now on Nintendo Switch 2:
body: Take a first look at content and features included in the first HD 2D FINAL FANTASY!

The pixel-art world of FINAL FANTASY returns in this reimagined adventure! The world is full of secrets, including the wandering swordmaster Gilgamesh, a Colosseum with deadly monsters and rewards to match, the Chamber of Arms with formidable foes sealed within legendary weapons, and a showdown with Ultima Weapon. Try out the first chapter in the free demo!
Visit Nintendo.com for more info:
